## Blocks become Python {#blocks}

<iframe class="stem-frame" data-src="embeds/blocks.html" title="Blocks and Python"></iframe>

::: notes
Press **Run**: the program counts from 1 to 5 and says which numbers are even. On the right is **the same program in Python**. Change a block and watch the Python change.

Try: change *to 5* to *to 10*. Change *even* to *a multiple of 3* (the remainder of n ÷ 3). Drag in a new **print** block from *Text*.

This uses **Blockly** (free, from Google; the same blocks as Code.org and Scratch), saved in the course, so it works without the internet. The page is `embeds/blocks.html`.
:::

## Build the line of code

::: {.sentence-builder}
- print / ( / name / ) | Show the value of name on the screen.
- for / i / in / range(5) / : | Repeat the code under it 5 times.
- if / score / > / 10 / : | Only do the next part when score is more than 10.
- total / = / total / + / 1 | Add 1 to total.
:::

::: notes
**Build the sentence**, used for code. Each `/` marks one tile. Ask students to read each line aloud in plain English once it's built.
:::

## Find the biggest number

::: {.put-in-order first="First" last="Last"}
- Look at the first number. Call it "biggest".
- Look at the next number.
- If it is bigger than "biggest", it becomes "biggest".
- Repeat until there are no numbers left.
- Say "biggest". It is the answer.
:::

::: notes
An **algorithm** is a step-by-step plan. Put the steps in order, then act it out: give five students number cards and walk along the line.
:::

## Coding words

::: {.matching}
- algorithm | A step-by-step plan to solve a problem
- loop | Code that repeats
- variable | A named box that stores a value
- if | Code that makes a choice
- function | Steps with a name, to use again and again
- bug | A mistake in a program
:::
